drhp.business: SDHI operates an integrated shipyard that constructs commercial vessels (chemical tankers and dual-fuel ammonia bulk carriers) and defence vessels (a naval training ship for the Royal Navy of Oman), and also undertakes ship repair and refit assignments. Customers span international commercial shipowners and foreign government defence buyers, alongside the Indian maritime and defence ecosystem. The Company acquired the shipyard through a corporate insolvency resolution process and describes itself as a single segment company.

The Company states it has already impaired this investment and, although it continues to hold 100% of ECPL's equity, it has assessed that it does not have control over ECPL under Ind AS 110.

risks.note: International shipyards, particularly in China, South Korea and Japan, benefit from significant government subsidies, making it challenging for Indian yards to compete on pricing and delivery timelines - a structural pricing disadvantage for a yard bidding for international contracts.

Large, technically complex builds involve stringent delivery schedules, multi-vendor coordination and engineering integration challenges, which management says may impact execution timelines and project profitability. This is the dominant risk for a company whose entire near-term value rests on delivering a newly won order book.
risks.risk: Execution and project delivery risk on complex shipbuilding projects

risks.note: Critical marine equipment, propulsion systems, navigation systems and specialised components continue to have import dependency, exposing the business to currency fluctuations, supply disruptions and procurement delays.
risks.risk: Dependence on imported equipment and components

risks.note: Fluctuations in prices of steel, specialty alloys and marine equipment can adversely impact project margins, particularly on fixed-price contracts - the contract form used for the vessel orders in hand.
risks.risk: Raw material price volatility on fixed-price contracts

risks.note: Evolving global regulations on emissions, vessel efficiency, environmental standards and safety compliance may require continuous operational and technological upgrades, i.e. recurring compliance capex and design rework.
Operations near coastal areas are exposed to weather-related disruptions such as cyclones, flooding or heavy monsoons, affecting project schedules.
risks.risk: Natural disasters and climate risk at a coastal facility

risks.note: The MD&A states the Company is a single segment company, so there is no segmental diversification to absorb a downturn or an execution problem in shipbuilding.

Management describes FY 2025-26 as a year of strengthening and formalising internal financial controls alongside expanding operational scale, and states that while the controls in place are considered adequate, 'further improvements are ongoing' - a control-maturity gap relative to the step-up in scale.
risks.risk: Internal financial control framework still being built out
